title: Cookie Tin
shortDescription: Prize savings on Cookie Chain. Your deposit cannot be lost, and one saver wins the pot.
description: Cookie Tin is a savings vault on Cookie Chain where the deposit can never be lost and the prize is somebody else's money. A saver puts COOK into a tin and it comes back in full whenever they ask: there is no lending it out, no trading it, and no instruction in the program that moves lamports out of a tin to anybody but the owner of that position. Principal and prize money live in entirely separate program accounts, so paying a prize out of another saver's deposit is structurally impossible rather than merely checked, and withdrawal stays open even while the protocol is paused. What savers play for is a pool that a sponsor funds on top. Tins pay out in two shapes: streaming, where everyone earns continuously weighted by amount and time held, and lucky, where each wallet gets exactly one entry so a 1 COOK deposit and a 1,000 COOK deposit have identical odds and the largest wallet does not simply win. The lucky draw settles against the hash of a slot that did not exist when the draw was requested, and finalizing is bounded to a 300 slot window so nobody can stall until a hash they have already seen comes back into reach. Running the draw is permissionless, so a closed tin never waits on an absent creator to pay out. Gas is covered throughout by a sponsor vault, which means a wallet holding exactly zero COOK can deposit, withdraw and collect, and the relayer that fronts those fees has no authority over any vault and can reclaim at most 0.005 COOK per transaction, enforced on chain.
